claims.claim: For a fixed legal finite-horizon policy on finite alphabets, exact target decoding in every active context is possible if and only if complete observed transcript supports are disjoint across different target classes.
claims.boundary: Policy-specific. It neither proves that a separating legal policy exists nor validates an estimated transcript kernel. Positive KL without support separation is insufficient for finite exactness.

claims.claim: For a fixed legal policy, fixed-prior and rectangular robust expectations agree for every bounded path loss if and only if the induced closed convex path-law family is stable under positive-history pasting.
claims.boundary: The equivalence is policywise and donor-derived. A posterior-local minimax recursion generates the stated rectangular hull only when its admissible nature moves are exactly the induced positive-history conditional continuation families with independent historywise pasting; an unspecified local worst-posterior rule need not do so.
